correctness.rationale: The frozen proof at RESULT.md lines 33–35 is invalid as written: inserting 0 between the two 1s of the layered word 0011 gives 00101, with two noncontiguous blocks, and deleting a member of another block can close a gap. In that example the layered deletion results 0001 and 0011 have different compositions. The replacement at /workspace/repairs/4/RESULT.md proves the required distinction in general and retains the formula, extrema and attainment counts. For two valid old-block deletions from distinct blocks, any noncontiguous block must be one of the two. If either is noncontiguous the other must be as well: its deleted member is an isolated gap between runs of the first, but is in a block of size at least two. The deleted members then must be adjacent and are the interior positions of a segment X^u Y X Y^v; deleting either one gives different ordered compositions (u+1,v) and (u,v+1). Thus distinct-block deletions cannot collide for a fixed source. Same-block collisions require a block of precisely two separated occurrences and contiguous intervening singleton blocks, because the intervening length sequence must agree after moving a part of size one from front to back. Each singleton-run pair yields exactly one such double history and there are no triple histories. The other losses are n for layered old-block insertions and L per run of length L for new-singleton insertions; interior singleton insertions in nonsingleton blocks have unique histories. The repaired optimization uses a strict decrease when borrowing one unit from a part of size at least three to split or shorten a singleton run, balanced lengths for the minimum penalty and strict superadditivity for the maximum including k=1. This reconstructs all boundary cases and optimizer counts. The frozen checker was inspected, not run; its recorded finite evidence covers through n=10 and does not establish the repaired proof.
